skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through safe git worktree setup with directory selection, .gitignore checks, setup commands, baseline tests, and status reporting.
skill.summary: Create isolated git worktrees before starting feature work.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown formatting, documented git commands, or path references rather than executable package code. Manual review found SKILL.zip contains only the same SKILL.md, but the skill still has contextual risk from automatic setup commands and automatic commits.

remediation.issue: Automatic project setup and baseline tests can execute repository scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before install, build, or test commands. Warn users when the repository is untrusted.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to commit .gitignore changes automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before editing .gitignore and before creating a commit. Show the intended change first.

remediation.issue: The global hidden worktree location may surprise users.
remediation.suggestion: Make the global location opt-in and validate the expanded path before creating a worktree.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Project Setup Executes Repository Scripts
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to auto-detect project files and run dependency installation, builds, and tests. In an untrusted repository, those commands can execute repository-controlled scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 101-130 directly instruct running package, build, and test commands. These commands commonly execute project-controlled hooks, so the risk is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Commit Without Explicit User Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to add a worktree pattern to .gitignore and commit the change when the pattern is missing. That can modify repository history without a clear approval step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 62-67 explicitly say to add the ignore rule and commit it before proceeding. No separate user approval step is included.

content.value_statement: Feature work can disrupt the current checkout and hide baseline issues. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through isolated git worktree setup.
actual_capabilities: Finds an existing .worktrees or worktrees directory before choosing a location.
Checks CLAUDE.md for a project worktree directory preference.
Verifies .gitignore before using project-local worktree folders.
Creates a new git worktree for a named branch.
Detects common project files and runs setup and test steps.
Reports the worktree path and baseline test status.
limitations: Requires a Git repository that supports worktrees.
Can execute project-defined install or test scripts in the target repository.
Does not diagnose failing tests without additional user direction.
Global worktree placement depends on the user shell and path conventions.

use_cases.title: Start Feature Work Safely
use_cases.description: Create a branch worktree so feature changes do not disturb the active checkout.

use_cases.title: Prepare AI Implementation
use_cases.description: Set up an isolated workspace before asking an AI assistant to implement a plan.

use_cases.title: Review Multiple Branches
use_cases.description: Keep several branches available at once for review, testing, or comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated git worktree for my next feature. Use existing project conventions and ask me if no worktree directory is configured.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up and Test a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for branch feature/auth-refresh. Verify the local worktree folder is ignored, install project dependencies, and run the baseline tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Before Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Before implementing the approved plan, create a git worktree. Follow the repository preference, report the path, and stop if baseline tests fail.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Worktree Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository's worktree conventions, .gitignore rules, and setup commands. Recommend a safe worktree creation sequence before making changes.

output_examples.input: Create a worktree for the login feature.
output_examples.output: Selected the existing project-local worktree directory, verified it is ignored, created the feature branch workspace, and reported passing tests.

output_examples.input: Prepare an isolated workspace before implementation.
output: Confirmed the repository root and project name.
Stopped after baseline tests failed and asked for direction.

output_examples.input: Help me review two branches without switching my main checkout.
output_examples.output: Created separate worktree guidance for each branch and explained how to keep the main checkout unchanged.

best_practices: Confirm the target branch name and feature scope before creating the worktree.
Review install and test commands before running them in untrusted repositories.
Keep project-local worktree folders ignored by Git.
anti_patterns: Running dependency installation in an untrusted repository without approval.
Continuing implementation after baseline tests fail.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides an AI assistant through creating an isolated git worktree for feature work.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Codex, Claude, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it create a new branch?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow creates a worktree tied to a new named branch.

faq.question: Why does it check .gitignore?
faq.answer: It helps prevent project-local worktree contents from being tracked by Git.

faq.question: Does it run project commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes setup and test steps, so review commands before using untrusted repositories.

faq.question: What happens if baseline tests fail?
faq.answer: The skill tells the assistant to report the failure and ask before continuing.
